lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: describe the composition of the blood: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma
understand the role of plasma in the transport of carbon dioxide, digested food, urea, hormones and heat energy
understand how adaptations of red blood cells make them suitable for the transport of oxygen, including shape, the absence of a nucleus and the presence of haemoglobin

primer.text: Blood looks like one red liquid but is really a suspension: cells and fragments riding a straw-coloured carrier. Plasma hauls the dissolved cargo, red cells grab the oxygen, white cells fight, platelets patch. This note assigns each component its job and its shape.

modules.title: The Four Components of Blood
modules.opening: Blood suspends red cells, white cells and platelets in plasma, which fills over half the volume, with red cells claiming most of the remainder and the white cells and platelets sharing the small rest.
keyPoints: Plasma is the straw-coloured liquid carrying everything.
Red cells are biconcave discs without a nucleus, packed with haemoglobin.
White cells are large, nucleated defensive cells.
Plasma occupies over half of the blood's volume.

low.restatement: Plasma carries; red cells ferry oxygen; white cells defend; platelets patch holes.
low.analogy: A river barge: the river (plasma), the cargo crews (red cells), the guards (white cells) and the repair dinghies (platelets).
low.examPointer: Reproduce the table's structure column if asked to 'describe the composition'.

medium.restatement: Each component's structure anticipates its function: no nucleus buys haemoglobin space, a large nucleus runs defence chemistry, fragment status lets platelets jam into any gap.
medium.analogy: A well-cut crew uniform: every shape exists because of the job it must do.
medium.examPointer: Volume proportions get asked: over half plasma, most of the rest red cells.

modules.title: Plasma, the Cargo Liquid
modules.opening: Plasma transports the dissolved and suspended cargo of the blood: carbon dioxide from the cells to the lungs, digested food and ions from the gut, urea toward the kidneys, hormones to their targets, and heat toward the skin.
keyPoints: Carbon dioxide rides dissolved in plasma toward the lungs.
Digested food and mineral ions travel from the small intestine.
Urea is delivered to the kidneys for removal.
Hormones reach their target organs through the plasma.
Heat energy moves to cooler parts or to the skin for loss.

low.restatement: Plasma carries gas, food, ions, urea, hormones and heat around the body.
low.analogy: A delivery van's cargo bay: everything loose rides in the same compartment.
low.examPointer: Learn the five cargoes by name; one missing item costs the mark.

medium.restatement: Every listed cargo travels dissolved or suspended in the aqueous plasma, which is why the blood can service respiration, excretion, coordination and temperature control simultaneously.
medium.analogy: One river serving every factory along its banks.
medium.examPointer: Pair each cargo with its destination: lungs, cells, kidneys, targets, skin.

modules.title: Red Cells Built for Oxygen
modules.opening: Red blood cells are oxygen ferries whose three adaptations work together: haemoglobin binds the gas, the absent nucleus frees space for it, and the biconcave disc shape enlarges the surface for rapid exchange.
keyPoints: Haemoglobin binds oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin.
No nucleus leaves more room for haemoglobin.
The biconcave disc shape raises the surface-area-to-volume ratio.
Oxygen diffuses in and out quickly because of that shape.
Their cargo reaches every respiring cell in the body.

low.restatement: Red cells carry oxygen using haemoglobin, no nucleus and a dimpled disc shape.
low.analogy: A van with every seat stripped out except the cargo racks.
low.examPointer: Name all three adaptations together when a question asks 'how are they adapted'.

medium.restatement: The three traits are a package: binding chemistry, packing space and exchange geometry each raise the oxygen delivery rate.
medium.analogy: A courier with the right satchel, a light frame and a short driveway.
medium.examPointer: If asked for the shape's advantage, quote the surface-area-to-volume ratio wording.

glossary.definition: The straw-coloured liquid suspending the blood's cells and carrying its dissolved cargo.
The red-cell protein that binds oxygen into oxyhaemoglobin.
Dented on both faces, the red-cell shape that enlarges its surface.
The nitrogen waste carried in plasma to the kidneys.
